1. Heard Sri Saurabh Yadav, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri Devesh Vikram, learned
Additional Chief Standing Counsel for the State-respondent and Ms. Akanksha Gaur, learned
counsel appearing for National Highways Authority of India.
2.
The instant writ petition is preferred for quashing the impugned order dated 07.08.2025 passed by respondent no.3.

A mandamus has also been sought commanding respondent no.2 to compensate the petitioner for an area of 238 sq. meter of Gata No.840 situated at Village Eht,
Pargana Orai, District Jalaun.

3. The record reflects that grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent-NHAI had not compensated the petitioner for an area measuring 238 sq. meter of Gata No.840 situated at Village Eht, Pargana Orai, District Jalaun.
The said land had been purchased by the petitioner through a sale deed dated 01.06.2004 from one Raja Ram, Lallu Ram and Ram Kumar all sons of Channe.
The said land was acquired by the National Highway Authority of India under the National Highways Act, 2005 (in short called as "the Act, 1956") in the year 2004.

4. It appears from the compendium that the petitioner had previously invoked the writ jurisdiction by preferring Writ-C No.11979 of 2024 for release of compensation, which was disposed of by the Division Bench of this Court vide order dated 29.04.2024 giving relief to the petitioner to approach the competent authority with fresh representation alongwith no objection certificate from the vendors and such other documents as may be required, by respondent no.3 therein.
5. As, it is informed that later on the authority had passed the order on 13.07.2024, which was again subject matter of challenge in Writ-C No.39652 of 2024 filed before this Court.

The Division Bench again vide judgment and order dated 20.12.2024 quashed the order dated 13.07.2024, which was impugned in the said writ petition, and matter was relegated to the competent authority, Jalaun at Orai, under the Land Acquisition Act, to pass fresh order.
6.

Learned counsel for the petitioner, in this backdrop, submits that the order passed by the competent authority, which is impugned in this writ petition, is per se unsustainable as earlier, the authority at its own motion had passed an order and quantified the amount as per the residential circle rate on 25.10.2018 and in spite of the repeated request, ignoring the factual aspect of the matter, the order impugned has been passed.
He submits that since 2005 the petitioner is pressing the relief and, till date, the valuable rights have been denied to the petitioner in arbitrary manner.

sentences.text: Such situation has impelled the petitioner to invoke writ jurisdiction.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents opposed the relief and submits that once the matter has been relegated by the Division Bench vide order dated 20.12.2024, the competent authority, after giving an opportunity to all the stakeholder, has decided the matter and held that the compensation is to be quantified as per agricultural circle rate.
Hence, the order impugned warrant no interference.

Alternatively, it has also been stated that against the order impugned, the petitioner is having efficacious remedy to press the relief before the arbitrator under Section 3G(5) of the Act,
1956.
The writ petition is therefore, devoid of merit and liable to be dismissed on the ground of efficacious alternative remedy.

8. Considering the factual situation and without indulging into the merit of the case, as the petitioner is agitating the matter since 2005, in the interest of justice, it is provided that in case the petitioner invokes the proceedings before the arbitrator within two weeks from today, the same shall be considered on merits, ignoring the delay and laches, if any, and the said proceedings shall also be finalized expeditiously.
9.
With the aforesaid observation, this writ petition stands disposed of.
(Anish Kumar Gupta,J.) (Mahesh Chandra Tripathi,J.) September 3, 2025
